title: Transforming search and discovery using LLMs — Tejaswi & Vinesh, Instacart
talk_summary: Instacart's search team improved query understanding and discovery by using LLMs, but only after injecting Instacart-specific behavioral context (top-converting categories, subsequent queries) into prompts, because raw LLM world knowledge mismatched user intent. They precompute LLM outputs offline in batch for head/torso queries and serve from cache, falling back to cheaper models for the tail, and they stress that automated evaluation was harder and more important than expected.

takeaways.technique: Inject behavioral/domain context into prompts instead of relying on model world knowledge
takeaways.what_they_do: They feed the LLM the top-K converting categories for each query (and later subsequent queries users issued) as context, which fixed mismatches like 'protein' meaning shakes/bars to users but chicken/tofu to the LLM.

takeaways.technique: Precompute LLM outputs offline in batch and serve from cache; fall back to cheap models for the tail
takeaways.what_they_do: Because Instacart has a fat head/torso of queries, they batch-computed LLM outputs for those offline, cached them in a feature store, and served lookups online with negligible latency, falling back to existing/distilled models for the long tail.

takeaways.technique: Distill to a smaller model for the long tail
takeaways.what_they_do: For the very long tail where they fall back to old models, they are replacing them with a distilled Llama model to get better quality than the legacy models at acceptable cost.

takeaways.technique: Automated LLM-as-judge evaluation pipeline, built early
takeaways.what_they_do: They built an automated evaluation pipeline using an LLM as a judge to check both correctness (no hallucination) and adherence to product requirements, and said this was harder and more important than anticipated and discovered late.

takeaways.technique: Consolidate many narrow models into one unified model for consistency
takeaways.what_they_do: They note query understanding is a chain of many models and that managing them is complex; consolidating into one SLM/LLM makes results more consistent, citing a case where a brand tagger and spell corrector disagreed and produced confusing results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: consolidating all of these into an SLM or a or maybe a large language model uh can make the results a lot more consistent

takeaways.technique: Simple prompts plus candidate generation and downstream ranking/validation
takeaways.what_they_do: They kept prompts very simple, generated candidate categories, then did ranking and downstream validation rather than trying to encode all logic in the prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's a bunch of uh ranking and downstream validation that happens. But essentially that that was what we did. We generated a bunch of candidates uh rank candidates
